verdict.rationale: Yubico's own mobile SDK docs confirm that NFC-enabled YubiKeys work with phones. On Android, YubiKit supports NFC keys and provides a FIDO2/WebAuthn client with WebView integration. On iOS, the library can request an OTP from an NFC YubiKey using an NFC-enabled device. However, in-app support depends on app developers integrating these SDKs, and native mobile-browser passkey authentication over NFC is not documented. missing for 10: documented NFC FIDO2/passkey authentication in mobile browsers (Safari/Chrome), iOS NFC FIDO2 rather than OTP only, hands-on or community corroboration of tap-to-phone use.

support.subject: As a power user, I can tap the key on my phone over NFC to authenticate in mobile browsers and apps

citations.quote: YubiKit is an Android library provided by Yubico to enable YubiKey support in Android apps. Both USB and NFC-enabled YubiKeys are supported.
The library supports NFC-enabled YubiKeys and provides the APIs to request an OTP (Yubico OTP or HOTP) from the NFC YubiKeys using a NFC-enabled iOS device.
provides a high-level FIDO2/WebAuthn client with built-in UI components, WebView integration, and customizable theming
